A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same analytic-concept framework for articulated-object manipulation. All ten pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations, and references, are readable. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix. Some revised experimental settings remain ambiguous, but the material supports comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulated manipulation experiments on PartNet-Mobility, gripper-versus-suction comparisons, and physical-robot experiments on eight household objects in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: V2 reports simulated and physical-robot results in Tables 1–3, plus original grasp-parameter controls and module-level error analysis in Tables 4–5.

M1.justification: The GPT-4o/Grounded-SAM pipeline, structural and pose estimators, conditional-GAN grasp selection, analytic force computation, and training objectives are retained. V2 expands the geometric and force-parameter illustrations and describes suction adaptation, but parameterized manipulation knowledge and suction evaluation already appear in v1. These changes do not establish a new algorithm or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 15 PartNet-Mobility categories, eight physical-object tasks, and gripper/suction scenarios. However, v1 explicitly evaluates pushing and pulling separately, while v2's simulation settings and tables no longer identify the action mix. The PDFs do not establish whether task coverage changed or only its reporting was consolidated.

E2.justification: V2 adds A3VLM to the main simulation comparison alongside Where2Act, Where2Explore, GAPartNet, and ManipLLM. It also adds A3VLM to the suction comparison and replaces ManipLLM with A3VLM in the physical-robot comparison. These changes materially revise the comparison set across the principal evaluations.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a random grasp-parameter control and sequential ground-truth substitution of pipeline modules, with the latter restricted to training categories. These substantially extend the evaluation design. Its simulation description also specifies five interactions per action proposal, whereas v1 specifies ten trials per object; the relationship between these different quantities is unexplained.

E4.justification: Beyond the end-effector comparison already present in v1, v2 adds two substantive analyses in Section 5.3. Table 4 tests learned grasp-parameter estimation against random sampling, and Table 5 progressively substitutes ground-truth module outputs to diagnose system errors. Neither analysis appears in v1.

E5.justification: V1 explicitly reports ten simulation trials per testing object; v2 omits that repetition count and instead reports an interaction budget, which is a different quantity. Both retain ten trials per physical task. Neither version reports seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Simulation results are substantially replaced: v1 Table 1 reports proposed-method train/test averages of 41.08/40.33 for pushing and 25.97/25.50 for pulling; v2 reports 42.5/40.8 without that breakdown. V2 also adds category-level suction results and Tables 4–5. The proposed method's physical-robot rates remain unchanged. These revisions do not establish like-for-like performance gains. V2's stated 15.2% training-category improvement also disagrees with Table 1's 42.5 versus 37.4, which implies approximately 13.6%.

T1.justification: Neither version presents theorems or proofs. The discriminator and generator objectives in v1 Equations 1–2 are retained inline in v2, and the geometric grounding mathematics is substantively unchanged. Added SE(3) notation and expanded geometric explanations do not introduce new mathematical results.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that analytic concepts bridge semantic commonsense knowledge and physical robot control, enabling accurate, generalizable articulated-object manipulation. The three principal contributions and conclusion retain their meaning. MLLM terminology clarifies the multimodal model already used in v1; interpretability remains claimed in v2's introduction despite its omission from the abstract.

C2.justification: V2 adds a substantive failure interpretation absent from v1: sequential oracle substitutions identify structural-parameter and 6-DoF pose estimation as principal bottlenecks, with errors causing collisions or misaligned grasps. It also interprets the sampling control as evidence for analytic grasp constraints and an additional benefit from visual parameter estimation. V1 primarily explains successful performance through combining language-model reasoning with physical grounding.

D1.justification: V2 removes v1 Section 4.5's training-data preparation recipe, including concept annotation, simulator rendering, URDF-derived supervision, and successful/failed grasp sampling. Explicit average-pooling and ReLU details and the prospective concept-release statement also disappear. V2 newly reports 972 objects and the five-interaction budget, but these disclosures do not replace the removed data-generation information. The omissions concern documentation, not demonstrated changes to training or resource availability.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion of A3VLM and citations to newer robotics work, including Octo, OpenVLA, ReKep, OmniManip, and SoFAR. It adds the GPT-4o system card and removes the GPT-2 comparison. These update the research context while retaining the central positioning around grounding semantic knowledge through analytic concepts.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, concept descriptions, and method explanations undergo extensive rewriting and compression. V2 emphasizes MLLM terminology, renames method subsections, nests simulation settings and results under Section 5.1, and creates a dedicated ablation section. The contribution list and author/affiliation block are also reformatted and revised.

P2.justification: V1 Figures 1–2 are merged and redrawn as v2 Figure 1; the concept and pipeline diagrams are substantially redesigned. Simulation tables gain colored category headers and different structures: the main table loses separate push/pull blocks, and suction results gain category-level columns. Two new analysis tables are added. The physical examples are retained as v2 Figure 4 rather than constituting new visual evidence.

improvement.justification: A3VLM comparisons and the new grasp-control and error-breakdown studies provide useful evidence about component effectiveness and failure sources that v1 lacked. This supports a limited overall improvement. The benefits are tempered by removal of the training-data recipe and separate push/pull results, unclear continuity of the simulation protocol, and the inconsistent training-improvement percentage. Higher revised simulation scores alone do not establish better paper quality.
